page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 96 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, translating to 7.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 5669 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top 10% placement in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is exceptionally strong, with cached read-only bandwidth reaching 10,897.38 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 205.78 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10%, processing 170.49 million operations per second.

While multi-threaded and memory-intensive workloads excel, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. The ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX, which limits its suitability for legacy software requiring these vector extensions. However, the high physical core density and substantial memory allocation provide excellent qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads, offering massive resource density without hyperthreading overhead.

This server is highly optimized for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, static web serving, and software compilation pipelines. Additionally, its top-tier multi-threaded performance makes it suitable for specific parallel processing tasks, such as ray tracing and text generation for medium to large language models.
description: The Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is an ARM64-based virtual machine from the Epdsv6 family, featuring 96 dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM and 5669 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this server delivers top-tier multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database execution speeds, as evidenced by its top 10% ranking in multi-core stress-ng and Redis SET operations. While single-core performance and vector instruction support are limited, the instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for parallel workloads. It is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
